name: frontend-design
when_to_use: When architecting distinctive, production-grade frontend web interfaces, designing responsive layouts, or configuring design token systems.
when_not_to_use: When writing headless backend services, database migrations, or server-side CLI scripts.
example: Design an accessible, responsive dashboard layout using CSS custom properties with zero horizontal overflow at 390px.

name: accessibility-review
when_to_use: When auditing user interfaces for W3C WCAG 2.2 AA compliance, keyboard operability, color contrast, and proper ARIA semantics.
when_not_to_use: When developing non-interactive backend APIs, scheduled batch jobs, or internal CLI tools.
example: Audit the authentication and checkout forms against WCAG 2.2 AA criteria and write automated axe-core checks.

name: design-handoff
when_to_use: When translating UI/UX mockups, typography scales, spacing tokens, and component specifications into clean frontend component implementations.
when_not_to_use: When drafting backend business domain models, database indexing strategies, or server routing.
example: Extract spacing tokens, color values, and responsive breakpoint rules from design specs into our Tailwind theme configuration.

name: design-critique
when_to_use: When evaluating an existing user interface for visual hierarchy, clutter, readability, inconsistent type scales, and cognitive overload.
when_not_to_use: When conducting low-level code review for algorithmic complexity or memory leak profiling.
example: Review this dashboard view and identify the top three visual hierarchy defects that confuse first-time users.

name: ux-copy
when_to_use: When writing user-facing button labels, empty states, error messages, form field placeholders, and onboarding tooltips.
when_not_to_use: When writing internal technical variable names, system logs, or developer code comments.
example: Rewrite these five cryptic HTTP error messages into clear, actionable user feedback strings.

name: deep-research
when_to_use: When conducting comprehensive technical investigations into competing architectures, complex compliance standards, or unfamiliar third-party APIs.
when_not_to_use: When solving straightforward syntax bugs or implementing well-understood CRUD endpoints.
example: Investigate production trade-offs between WebSockets and Server-Sent Events for our real-time notification engine.

name: user-research
when_to_use: When formulating customer interview protocols, identifying user pain points, and discovering manual workarounds before building software.
when_not_to_use: When designing database schemas, query indexing, or CI/CD pipelines.
example: Draft a non-leading 30-minute user interview script to uncover manual accounting reconciliation friction.

name: research-synthesis
when_to_use: When aggregating multiple user interview transcripts or stakeholder feedback notes into prioritized themes and problem statements.
when_not_to_use: When analyzing automated code coverage or performance profiling traces.
example: Synthesize these five interview transcripts into a prioritized pain-point matrix with supporting direct user quotes.

name: humanizer
when_to_use: When reviewing documentation, commit logs, and PR descriptions to remove robotic, repetitive AI filler words and restore crisp engineering prose.
when_not_to_use: When editing machine-readable configuration files, JSON schemas, or strict TypeScript types.
example: Review this system documentation and remove marketing fluff, redundant adverbs, and robotic transitional phrases.

name: token-efficiency-audit
when_to_use: When optimizing prompt size, file contexts, and coding agent session boundaries to prevent context blowup and runaway API costs.
when_not_to_use: When drafting high-level product vision statements or initial brainstorming sessions.
example: Audit our prompt templates and repository context files to reduce token payload by 40% without losing structural constraints.

name: skill-creator
when_to_use: When authoring reusable agent skill bundles (SKILL.md, references, scripts) to institutionalize team patterns for coding agents.
when_not_to_use: When completing a single ad-hoc bugfix that requires no standardized procedural workflow.
example: Package our database zero-downtime migration rules and verification checks into a reusable agent skill folder.

name: docx
when_to_use: When generating or parsing formal enterprise documents, business requirement dossiers, or customer statements of work in Microsoft Word format.
when_not_to_use: When writing in-repo software documentation, which should always be version-controlled Markdown.
example: Convert our validated PRD and non-functional requirements into a formal DOCX proposal for enterprise procurement.

name: xlsx
when_to_use: When modeling complex financial estimates, cost projections, capacity spreadsheets, or tabular performance benchmark datasets.
when_not_to_use: When storing transactional relational application data, which belongs in PostgreSQL.
example: Generate an infrastructure cost estimation model comparing multi-AZ container runtimes across traffic tiers in XLSX format.

name: pptx
when_to_use: When preparing slide decks for executive stakeholder alignment, milestone reviews, or architecture approval committees.
when_not_to_use: When documenting detailed low-level software implementation steps for engineers.
example: Generate a concise 5-slide architecture summary deck for the Gate G1 executive scope-lock review.

name: pdf
when_to_use: When publishing immutable release certifications, security audit reports, or executive handoff sign-off packets.
when_not_to_use: When editing working engineering documents that need continuous team collaboration.
example: Export the completed SOC2 compliance checklist and security threat model into an immutable PDF audit artifact.

name: file-reading
when_to_use: When inspecting specific source files, package manifests, or logs with precise line-range targeting to conserve context tokens.
when_not_to_use: When dumping entire massive repositories into agent context without surgical targeting.
example: Read lines 45 through 120 of src/services/billing.ts to inspect the transaction boundary logic.

name: artifact-diagramming
when_to_use: When authoring Mermaid or SVG system diagrams, C4 models, sequence diagrams, and lifecycle state machines in documentation.
when_not_to_use: When explaining simple scalar configuration parameters that are clearer as a table or list.
example: Generate a Mermaid sequence diagram illustrating the JWT authentication handshake and token refresh flow.

name: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)
when_to_use: When setting up project operating rules, build/test commands, and architectural boundaries for autonomous coding agents.
when_not_to_use: When writing customer marketing materials or end-user facing product manuals.
example: Author a concise AGENTS.md file establishing the single-task rule, test commands, and commit message conventions.

name: GitHub Actions
when_to_use: When automating continuous integration, automated testing matrices, security scanning, container builds, and deployment workflows.
when_not_to_use: When running quick local feedback loops on developer laptops during active coding.
example: Write a GitHub Actions workflow with pinned action SHAs, OIDC authentication, and parallelized unit test matrix.

name: Testcontainers
when_to_use: When running automated integration tests against real databases (PostgreSQL, Redis) in disposable containers during CI and local testing.
when_not_to_use: When running fast, pure domain logic unit tests that should execute in under 10 milliseconds without container overhead.
example: Configure a Testcontainers setup in TypeScript that spins up a fresh PostgreSQL container for API route integration tests.
